title: Differential Facet Availability Semantics & Multi-Provider Comparison

claims.assertion: Multi-provider function comparison must force dimension status to 'unknown' with null counts when either side declares a required facet unavailable or when an empty facet lacks an explicit coverage declaration.
claims.evidence_quote: const availability = dossier.facet_availability?.[field]; if (availability?.available === false) return [`${field}: ${availability.reason}`]; return availability === undefined && count === 0 ? [`${field}: Provider did not declare coverage for this empty facet.`] : [];

claims.assertion: Absence of an artifact, entry, or property can only be formally claimed when the provider's inventory declares complete coverage, is not truncated, and omits zero entries; any other coverage state must yield 'unknown' rather than absence.
claims.evidence_quote: export const absenceClaimable = (coverage: { readonly status: string; readonly truncated?: boolean; readonly omitted_count?: number | null; }): boolean => coverage.status === 'complete' && coverage.truncated !== true && (coverage.omitted_count === undefined || coverage.omitted_count === 0);

claims.assertion: Comparing evidence produced by providers with differing representation formats (e.g. Ghidra vs Hopper assembly syntax) must record a 'providersDiffer' limitation and equate only structurally normalized projections, not raw provider text.
claims.evidence_quote: const providersDiffer = canonicalJson(left.evidence.provider, 'Function comparison') !== canonicalJson(right.evidence.provider, 'Function comparison'); ... conclusion_kind: input.providersDiffer ? 'contradiction' : 'derived_relationship'
